newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Skikda port hydrocarbon traffic up in H1.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Skikda port hydrocarbon traffic up in H1.

text.p: Algeria's Skikda port traffic of liquefied hydrocarbon rose 11 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 6.2 million tonnes compared to the same period last year, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Monday.

It quoted the port authority as saying that non-liquefied hydrocarbon transport in the port, one of Algeria's main outlets for oil and gas exports, declined five percent in the first quarter compared to the same period last year.
Algeria replies on the port of Skikda for more than 90 percent of its foreign currency earnings. The other port complex is in the western city of Oran.

Skikda port handled 39 percent more imported cereals in the first quarter and 70.5 percent in additional cargos of varied imported food products in the same period, said APS without giving specific figures.
While passenger traffic rose 23 percent to 3,874 travellers, the movement of vessels ebbed to 1,059 against 1,088 in the first quarter of 1996, it added.
